source.title: Feature: Generate engineering Technical Data Packages (TDPs) for Make-vs-Buy decisions
source.body:
## Objective
Implement a versioned **Technical Data Package (TDP)** workflow in foaMES so an engineering team can receive a controlled, decision-ready package for a **make-versus-buy** assessment of a part, assembly, process, tool, or equipment item.

The TDP must present the same technical baseline to internal manufacturing engineers and external suppliers, clearly separate facts from estimates, and preserve traceability from requirements through the final recommendation. The initial release should **support engineering judgment**, not automatically approve a sourcing decision.

## Scope and functional requirements

### 1. Package definition and source data
- Establish a TDP record associated with an item/assembly/project, revision, owner, decision scope, intended quantities/volumes, and required decision date.
- Capture functional/performance requirements, design inputs, assumptions, constraints, and open questions.
- Include applicable CAD models and neutral exports (e.g., STEP), 2D drawings/PDFs, specifications, material and finish requirements, critical dimensions/tolerances, interface definitions, and BOM with quantities, alternates, and revision references.
- Capture process and manufacturability inputs: candidate processes, routing/operations, tooling/fixtures, required equipment, setup and cycle times, production volume, capacity, yield/scrap, and any special handling.
- Capture quality and verification requirements: acceptance criteria, inspection/test plans, metrology requirements, relevant standards/compliance, required certifications, and critical-to-quality characteristics.
- Allow attachments or links to calculations, simulations, design reviews, risk/FMEA work, and existing engineering analyses, with provenance and version information.
- Mark every data element **required / optional / not applicable / unknown**, with a source and confidence/assumption where applicable.

### 2. Make-versus-buy evaluation worksheet
Provide side-by-side, editable and transparent comparison of:
- **Make:** internal process feasibility, engineering/NRE effort, capital and tooling, material/labor/overhead, maintenance, capacity utilization, lead time, ramp-up, yield, and quality risk.
- **Buy:** candidate suppliers/capabilities, RFQ scope and response, unit prices by volume, MOQ, NRE/tooling, logistics, lead time, quality history, supply continuity, and IP/data-sharing risk.
- **Both:** total cost of ownership across agreed volumes/time horizon, sensitivity/scenarios, schedule, control of critical know-how, compliance, and operational risks.
- Document the decision rationale, unresolved assumptions, reviewer comments, sign-off, and follow-up actions. Record the actual outcome separately from the recommendation.

Calculations must expose formulas, units, currency, quantity breaks, cost basis, and source dates; never present missing inputs as zero or imply unwarranted precision.

### 3. Package generation and handoff
- Produce a human-readable **PDF TDP** with cover/revision index, executive engineering summary, technical requirements, BOM/drawing index, process/quality sections, assumptions, risks, and an evaluation worksheet.
- Produce a **machine-readable manifest** (JSON or similar) describing item identity, revisions, document references, checksums, missing inputs, and package provenance. Allow a ZIP export containing permitted attachments plus the PDF and manifest.
- Support separate **internal** and **supplier-safe** export profiles. External exports must explicitly exclude confidential costing, internal risk assessments, protected IP, restricted drawings, and secrets unless authorized by policy.
- Capture who generated the package, when, from which baseline and attachments. Retain prior issued revisions and a change log.

### 4. Validation and governance
- Preflight completeness checks for critical engineering fields, conflicting revisions, missing/unreadable attachments, unit inconsistencies, unapproved documents, and unsupported cost assumptions.
- Provide a readiness state: **Draft -> Engineering Review -> Approved for Evaluation -> Issued**, with reasoned exceptions and audit history. No implied approval from a successful export alone.
- Integrate with foaMES item/BOM, document, validation, and manufacturing data where available; use adapters for CAD/CAE integrations (including planned FreeCAD, Onshape, and OpenFOAM) without blocking MVP on those integrations.
- Keep engineer/supervisor review and permissions explicit. Record approval for external distribution separately from technical approval.

## Suggested implementation slices
1. Define TDP schema, required-field profiles, source/revision tracking, and sample fixture.
2. Build data collection UI/API plus attachment registry and BOM/drawing index.
3. Build make/buy comparison worksheet with inspectable calculations and scenarios.
4. Add PDF/JSON/ZIP generator, redaction profiles, and validation preflight.
5. Add review/approval workflow, audit log, tests, and example handoff package.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Engineer can create a TDP from a foaMES item/assembly and complete it with manual inputs or available integrated data.
- [ ] Package includes revision-controlled requirements, BOM/drawing index, manufacturing feasibility, quality/verification requirements, and documented assumptions.
- [ ] Make and buy scenarios can be compared using auditable total-cost, lead-time, capacity, and risk inputs; unknown values remain visible.
- [ ] Validation identifies missing or inconsistent critical information and blocks **Issued** status until resolved or explicitly waived by an authorized reviewer.
- [ ] Export produces a reproducible PDF + manifest; optional ZIP includes allowed source files with checksums and references.
- [ ] Supplier-safe export does not leak internal-only fields or attachments; tests cover role-based access and redaction.
- [ ] Reviewers can record their recommendation, decisions, approvals, and rationale without overwriting the underlying engineering baseline.
- [ ] Automated tests cover schema validation, units/cost calculations, document revision mismatch, export completeness, and audit history.
- [ ] A sample TDP demonstrates one fabricated part with at least two manufacturing/sourcing alternatives and is usable by an engineering team without access to foaMES.

## Out of scope for initial release
Autonomous sourcing awards, PO issuance, supplier portal, full CAD/CAE model authoring, or automatic certification that a manufactured part meets requirements.
